title: Pleasing God · Chapter 4: God Sees Not As Man Sees
speaker: Joshua Heward-Mills
text:
Chapter 4

# God Sees Not As Man Sees

But the LORD said unto Samuel, Look not on his countenance, or on the height of his stature; because I have refused him: for the Lord seeth not as man seeth; for man looketh on the outward appearance, but the LORD looketh on the heart.

1 Samuel 16:7 (KJV)

God doesn't see how we see. One of the main things you have to do, if you're trying to please God, is shift how you assess things to match the way God assesses things. Otherwise you mark yourself and say, “God will be very happy with me.” Then the results come, and it's something else.

I once visited a well-known church with a few other people. I was deeply touched by the service and the faithfulness of the pastor. Afterwards, I walked around the church, looking carefully and making notes about the things I had learned.

Some people visit football stadiums when they go to a city. I notice churches. I have lived near a famous stadium without feeling any need to visit it, while a church can occupy my attention completely. At this particular church, I explored so enthusiastically that I once opened a door and found myself on the stage behind the worship leader as the next service was starting.

When we got into the car, I asked the people with me what they thought. Before I could share the things that had inspired me, they began criticising. They had noticed the things that were missing, the parts they thought too long or too short, and the ways they felt the service could have been better.

I was amazed. I might have given the church ninety-five per cent; they might have given it fifteen. We had attended the same service, but we were not seeing the same things.

They don't see how Joshua sees, and Joshua doesn't see how they see. So what is God's marking scheme? Which marking scheme do I use? My whole life is to serve God. Everybody can clap, but how will it be assessed?

But with me it is a very small thing that I should be judged of you, or of man’s judgment: yea, I judge not mine own self. For I know nothing by myself; yet am I not hereby justified: but he that judgeth me is the Lord. Therefore judge nothing before the time, until the Lord come, who both will bring to light the hidden things of darkness, and will make manifest the counsels of the hearts: and then shall every man have praise of God.

1 Corinthians 4:3-5 (KJV)

Paul says that human judgment is a small thing to him. He does not even treat his own assessment as the final one. The Lord is the One who judges.

I used to live my whole life by how people assessed me. You may think that means being a people pleaser, but there's another version: “How will I know I'm spiritual unless the pastor says I'm spiritual? How will I know I'm anointed unless some people say I'm anointed? How will I know I'm fulfilling my calling?” It may not be in the most worldly sense, but you actually assess yourself based on how other people see you.

When I look back at my life, I'm embarrassed about many things. As a pastor, I wonder what I was up to when I first became a pastor. What was I talking about? What was I doing? But at that time, when I examined myself, I felt I was doing this and doing that. We really are self-deceived about how we are.

Even judgments about beauty differ. A group of young men once came to tell me that their friend could not hope to marry a certain woman because she was the most beautiful woman in the church. I was surprised by their certainty. Later I asked my wife about it, and she agreed that the woman was very pretty. It was another reminder that people do not all assess things in the same way.

During my first year in law school, I went to study with a friend at another university. We exchanged the cases we were using in our courses. I thought my lecturers would be impressed by the additional authorities I had learned. Instead, I nearly failed the year. I received forty-one per cent, and my friend also received a low mark. We had failed to work according to the assessment expected of us.

In school, a composition might be assessed for content, expression, organisation, punctuation, and mechanical accuracy. At university, references became important in a way nobody had previously taught me. Knowing much is not enough if you do not know what is being marked.

What is God's marking scheme? That question matters before we reach eternity. He has called us to do what He has asked, not simply to attempt the largest thing we can imagine.

One church member may have a different assignment from a pastor and still be greater in eternity through faithfulness to that assignment. The question is not whether everybody had the same work. It is whether each person did what God wanted.

What terrifies me is to stand before God and hear, “I never asked you to do this.” You spent fifteen years doing it. Borrow God's eyes before you get to heaven. Assess yourself and pass His test before it's too late.

# 1. God sees the things hidden in darkness.

Therefore do not go on passing judgment before the time, but wait until the Lord comes who will both bring to light the things hidden in the darkness and disclose the motives of men’s hearts; and then each man’s praise will come to him from God.

1 Corinthians 4:5 (NASB 1995)

The first thing God uses to assess you is the things no one can see. What you've done, said, things you're doing that no one is aware of—the hidden things, unseen, unknown. When you want to start pleasing God, the first thing you have to know is that He sees what no one else sees. He knows what no one else knows.

People have confided painful experiences to me that they had never told anybody else. A human observer does not possess the whole story of a person's life. God does.

One day I got home from church and parked my car. It must have been about three in the morning. I sat there holding the steering wheel till about six or seven, saying things from my heart, deep things from my soul. No one saw, but God saw. I was hurt about something, and I was talking. You don't know, but it's part of my judgment. It's part of God's assessment of me.

I remember serving in a church and seeing a man with his hands lifted after worship. He seemed so absorbed that I hesitated to bring the moment to an end. After the service, I learned that the previous night he had violently assaulted his wife. The picture in front of us did not show what had happened at home. God saw both.

That is why outward spirituality cannot settle the question of whether God is pleased. We may appear one way in church while living very differently behind the scenes.

Somebody once brought me a recording of a person speaking strongly against me. As I discussed it with the person who brought it, I recognised that we could begin doing the very thing we were condemning. I suggested that we call the person rather than continue speaking behind the person's back. It is easy to forget that our own response is also being assessed.

I knew of a man who appeared to have an ordinary family life in church. Later, it became known that he had another wife and children in another city. He was maintaining two sets of family arrangements. What we could see was only part of the truth.

God's assessment is not confined to the final day. Our actions also bear fruit in this life.

While the earth remaineth, seedtime and harvest, and cold and heat, and summer and winter, and day and night shall not cease.

Genesis 8:22 (KJV)

We sow, and we reap. What we do has consequences. The fact that somebody does not announce what he knows does not mean that he does not know it. We must not mistake God's silence for ignorance.

When you see me teaching a Bible study, you see a pastor standing in front of people. But what am I really like? Am I loving when nobody is watching? Am I gentle, or am I harsh? Am I deceptive? Am I obedient to God? Can I receive correction?

But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, Meekness, temperance: against such there is no law.

Galatians 5:22-23 (KJV)

Those are serious questions. A public role does not answer them.

Human opinions can also differ greatly over the same events. I once spoke with a taxi driver in Germany whose judgments about wartime history were very different from the judgments I was accustomed to hearing. I was shocked by the conversation. It reminded me how strongly the account a person accepts can affect what that person sees. Human confidence is not the same as complete knowledge.

There are words in Scripture that should make us careful about private speech.

And Miriam and Aaron spake against Moses because of the Ethiopian woman whom he had married: for he had married an Ethiopian woman. And they said, Hath the LORD indeed spoken only by Moses? hath he not spoken also by us? And the LORD heard it.

Numbers 12:1-2 (KJV)

Miriam and Aaron were talking, and the Lord heard it. Their words were not invisible to Him because the conversation was private.

And when the people complained, it displeased the LORD: and the LORD heard it; and his anger was kindled; and the fire of the LORD burnt among them, and consumed them that were in the uttermost parts of the camp.

Numbers 11:1 (KJV)

The people's complaints displeased Him. We are discussing pleasing God, so we must also take seriously the things Scripture says displeased Him.

For in many things we offend all. If any man offend not in word, the same is a perfect man, and able also to bridle the whole body.

James 3:2 (KJV)

Control of the tongue reaches into the whole life. We need restraint even when nobody else will hear the words.

My pastor once told us of a night when he was about to speak out of strong feelings. His wife placed a hand on his chest and gently told him not to speak. Sometimes that is wise counsel: wait. Let the emotion pass before words create another problem.

We must also be humble when somebody else falls.

Brethren, if a man be overtaken in a fault, ye which are spiritual, restore such an one in the spirit of meekness; considering thyself, lest thou also be tempted.

Galatians 6:1 (KJV)

Restoration is the aim. Spiritual people are to help in a spirit of meekness, considering themselves. It is not an invitation to parade the wrong or to display how much better we are. If you are not spiritual enough to approach the matter humbly, do not rush into correcting somebody else.

God sees the fault, and He sees the heart with which you respond to it.

# 2. God sees the motives of the heart.

Motives don't have to do with what you are doing. They have to do with why. Why? You are preaching—good, but why? You say the Lord has called you—great, but why? You came to church, but why?

You preached—but why? You came to church—but why? You gave an offering, entered ministry, married, or helped somebody—but what were you seeking through it?

God's blessing on giving is real. But giving chiefly because I want to enrich myself is not the same motive as loving God and wanting to please Him. We should not hide the motive behind the religious appearance of an act.

Recently I sat in a meeting where the date of a programme was being discussed. I had a private reason for wanting a particular date kept free. I was able to offer convincing reasons why the programme should move. The reasons sounded good, but God knew the reason in my own heart. The outward discussion was not the whole matter.

Some people enter ministry because their studies or career have not worked out and ministry looks like a better option. The position may be spiritual, but the motive still needs to be examined.

Consider Abraham. God's call was accompanied by promises.

Now the LORD had said unto Abram, Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and from thy father’s house, unto a land that I will shew thee: And I will make of thee a great nation, and I will bless thee, and make thy name great; and thou shalt be a blessing: And I will bless them that bless thee, and curse him that curseth thee: and in thee shall all families of the earth be blessed.

Genesis 12:1-3 (KJV)

He was to leave his country and his father's house, and God would bless him and make him a blessing. Abraham had to believe what God said.

And he brought him forth abroad, and said, Look now toward heaven, and tell the stars, if thou be able to number them: and he said unto him, So shall thy seed be. And he believed in the LORD; and he counted it to him for righteousness.

Genesis 15:5-6 (KJV)

He believed the Lord, and it was counted to him for righteousness. Then came a different kind of test.

And it came to pass after these things, that God did tempt Abraham, and said unto him, Abraham: and he said, Behold, here I am. And he said, Take now thy son, thine only son Isaac, whom thou lovest, and get thee into the land of Moriah; and offer him there for a burnt offering upon one of the mountains which I will tell thee of. And Abraham rose up early in the morning, and saddled his ass, and took two of his young men with him, and Isaac his son, and clave the wood for the burnt offering, and rose up, and went unto the place of which God had told him.

Genesis 22:1-3 (KJV)

God asked for Isaac—the son through whom the promised future was to come. This was not a small thing. Abraham had waited for the promise, and the son he loved stood at the centre of it.

At that moment, the instruction was not presented as a new transaction with an immediate reward attached. God was asking for what Abraham loved. Would Abraham choose the gift or the Giver? Had he followed God for God Himself, or only for the thing he expected to receive?

Now we know it was a test. But Abraham—nobody texted him and said, “It's just a test.” No, no. What was God essentially saying? “Me or Isaac? Blessing or Blesser? Gift or Giver? Choose between us.” What's really in your heart? What were you really pursuing? Was it Me?

Think of what it would mean for somebody called into ministry to be asked to surrender everything that had been built around that call. If the visible reward disappeared, would the heart still choose Him?

And Abraham stretched forth his hand, and took the knife to slay his son. And the angel of the LORD called unto him out of heaven, and said, Abraham, Abraham: and he said, Here am I. And he said, Lay not thine hand upon the lad, neither do thou any thing unto him: for now I know that thou fearest God, seeing thou hast not withheld thy son, thine only son from me.

Genesis 22:10-12 (KJV)

“Now I know that thou fearest God.” The test brought the heart into view. Abraham had not withheld the son he loved.

And the angel of the LORD called unto Abraham out of heaven the second time, And said, By myself have I sworn, saith the LORD, for because thou hast done this thing, and hast not withheld thy son, thine only son: That in blessing I will bless thee, and in multiplying I will multiply thy seed as the stars of the heaven, and as the sand which is upon the sea shore; and thy seed shall possess the gate of his enemies; And in thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed; because thou hast obeyed my voice.

Genesis 22:15-18 (KJV)

God confirmed His blessing with an oath. The issue was not merely the visible activity of climbing a mountain or making an offering. It was the heart from which obedience came.

We need to guard the place from which our lives proceed.

Keep thy heart with all diligence; for out of it are the issues of life.

Proverbs 4:23 (KJV)

God looks at the heart. Let that direct your attention when you assess your life.

There is also a picture in the way the account continues. Genesis 22 records Abraham returning to the young men; later the narrative presents Isaac going out to meditate and meeting his bride. I see in that movement a picture pointing towards Christ and His coming for His bride. It is a picture drawn from the narrative, not an extra event stated in it.

So Abraham returned unto his young men, and they rose up and went together to Beer-sheba; and Abraham dwelt at Beer-sheba.

Genesis 22:19 (KJV)

And Isaac went out to meditate in the field at the eventide: and he lifted up his eyes, and saw, and, behold, the camels were coming. And Rebekah lifted up her eyes, and when she saw Isaac, she lighted off the camel. For she had said unto the servant, What man is this that walketh in the field to meet us? And the servant had said, It is my master: therefore she took a vail, and covered herself. And the servant told Isaac all things that he had done. And Isaac brought her into his mother Sarah’s tent, and took Rebekah, and she became his wife; and he loved her: and Isaac was comforted after his mother’s death.

Genesis 24:63-67 (KJV)

The main question remains the same: why are you doing what you do? I have been pastoring since 2010 and have spent years in full-time ministry. But the length of the service does not exempt the motive from examination.

# 3. The right steps cannot replace the right heart.

During 2020, I kept asking God what made the difference between one pastor and another. Was it how much a person prayed? How often the person fasted? I knew people who prayed intensely but whose ministries did not seem to go far. What was I missing?

This is the verse the Lord used to speak to me.

For the eyes of the LORD run to and fro throughout the whole earth, to shew himself strong in the behalf of them whose heart is perfect toward him. Herein thou hast done foolishly: therefore from henceforth thou shalt have wars.

2 Chronicles 16:9 (KJV)

God is looking throughout the earth. We may think we are searching for Him to use us, while He is searching for a heart towards which He can show Himself strong.

That changed something in me. I began to see that loving Him and having a heart given to Him reaches deeper than copying a set of steps.

My son, give me thine heart, and let thine eyes observe my ways.

Proverbs 23:26 (KJV)

People have the steps, the points, the principles, but they don't have the heart. I can teach you the steps of church growth. I can even give you the book, and you can passionately follow all the steps. But when you don't have the heart, God will assess your steps by the heart with which you're operating.

Simon saw that the Holy Spirit was given through the laying on of the apostles' hands. He recognised that something real was happening, desired the power, and offered money.

And when Simon saw that through laying on of the apostles’ hands the Holy Ghost was given, he offered them money, Saying, Give me also this power, that on whomsoever I lay hands, he may receive the Holy Ghost. But Peter said unto him, Thy money perish with thee, because thou hast thought that the gift of God may be purchased with money. Thou hast neither part nor lot in this matter: for thy heart is not right in the sight of God. Repent therefore of this thy wickedness, and pray God, if perhaps the thought of thine heart may be forgiven thee. For I perceive that thou art in the gall of bitterness, and in the bond of iniquity.

Acts 8:18-23 (KJV)

On the surface, somebody might identify familiar steps: recognise the gift, desire the grace, approach the minister, and bring something. But Peter did not receive the money and bless him. The problem was the heart. Simon thought the gift of God could be purchased.

The steps were all right, but the problem was your heart. “Your heart is not right.” You did all the right things, but your heart is not right. I'm sorry, you preach a better sermon than everybody. You're easier to understand. You work so hard. You've given your whole life. But what are you searching for? You want something. That's how God assesses us.

Abraham also refused a gift when he recognised what accepting it could allow somebody to claim.

And Abram said to the king of Sodom, I have lift up mine hand unto the LORD, the most high God, the possessor of heaven and earth, That I will not take from a thread even to a shoelatchet, and that I will not take any thing that is thine, lest thou shouldest say, I have made Abram rich:

Genesis 14:22-23 (KJV)

The presence of a gift is not, by itself, the whole spiritual question. There are times when receiving it would compromise the matter before God.

I have been young, and now am old; yet have I not seen the righteous forsaken, nor his seed begging bread.

Psalm 37:25 (KJV)

I have had different financial seasons in ministry, but I want to know God as my source. An outward transaction cannot take the place of that trust.

A minister once told me that the fellowship he had experienced with God in prison was so precious that he would rather return there than lose it. When you see the reach of somebody's ministry, do not assume that copying the outward methods will reproduce the heart from which it grew.

You don't love the people. You don't have a feeling for people. You can do all the steps, visitation, gathering, extended prayer, everything—but your heart! Our hearts are the most important thing. It's a heart issue.

There's no village God is not looking at, no seashore, no jungle. He's looking at all His servants from every corner of the globe, searching throughout the earth. He's looking for somebody to use greatly. But you can't love money, greatness, acclaim, your family, or your own self more than Him. He's looking for that complete heart.

Cornelius is another important example. As Peter listened to what had happened in his house, he recognised something about God's acceptance.

And Cornelius said, Four days ago I was fasting until this hour; and at the ninth hour I prayed in my house, and, behold, a man stood before me in bright clothing, And said, Cornelius, thy prayer is heard, and thine alms are had in remembrance in the sight of God. Send therefore to Joppa, and call hither Simon, whose surname is Peter; he is lodged in the house of one Simon a tanner by the sea side: who, when he cometh, shall speak unto thee. Immediately therefore I sent to thee; and thou hast well done that thou art come. Now therefore are we all here present before God, to hear all things that are commanded thee of God. Then Peter opened his mouth, and said, Of a truth I perceive that God is no respecter of persons: But in every nation he that feareth him, and worketh righteousness, is accepted with him.

Acts 10:30-35 (KJV)

God is no respecter of persons. In every nation, the one who fears Him and works righteousness is accepted with Him. Peter would not naturally have chosen that household, but God had seen what was happening there.

Spend time with Him. Being with God changes the heart. Do not merely collect methods while leaving your affections untouched.

# 4. Ask the Holy Spirit to change your heart.

The heart is deceitful above all things, and desperately wicked: who can know it? I the LORD search the heart, I try the reins, even to give every man according to his ways, and according to the fruit of his doings.

Jeremiah 17:9-10 (KJV)

The heart is a serious matter. It is also the place in which Christ is to dwell.

That Christ may dwell in your hearts by faith; that ye, being rooted and grounded in love,

Ephesians 3:17 (KJV)

Pray about your desires. Ask the Lord to make you love Him. This is why I keep encouraging people to have their quiet times. Being with Him does something that outward arrangements cannot do.

In October 2009, when I was nineteen, I went to South Korea for a church growth conference. I heard powerful preaching and sensed the anointing, but my own heart was not in a good place. I was not sure of my salvation. I wanted to return to the hotel, send messages to friends, and go on with the things I found attractive elsewhere.

The repeated church sessions felt burdensome to me. I could recognise that something good was happening, but I did not really want it.

During that visit we went to a prayer grotto in the mountains. There were small spaces where people could go in and pray. As I entered one, I found myself telling God honestly that I did not really like Him or His things. I could see that church and the Bible were good, but they did not attract me. The world did.

Then I asked Him to make me love Him. I wanted to want Him. I asked for a desire greater than the attraction I felt for everything else.

Later that year, in November, I was at a church event on a Friday night. I had intended to go somewhere else afterwards, but when the invitation to give my life to Christ came, I raised my hand. I told the people with me that I would not be going with them anymore. It was not the evening I had planned.

In January 2010, I went to university. A pastor visited me, brought a rice cooker, and showed me how to make rice. During the visit, I was invited to an all-night prayer meeting. I had given my life to Christ, but an all-night meeting still seemed a very demanding next step.

When Friday came, I looked at the rice cooker and received another message saying that they hoped to see me. I decided to go, partly to express my thanks. I arrived late, thinking that attending only part of the meeting would make it more manageable.

After some time, I went upstairs, sat on the floor, and slept. Later I returned to the meeting. A woman suggested that listening to a sermon while praying would help me stay awake. She put a message on my iPod. I remember being hesitant about connecting it to her computer because of the music that was on it. I was saved, but there was still much God was working on.

I began listening to a message about the missionary call while praying. Then something happened that I did not at first understand. I felt a strong movement in my chest and thought I might be having difficulty breathing. I went outside for fresh air into the cold winter night.

As I stood there, I heard myself telling God that I loved Him. I would serve Him with my whole life. There was nothing in the world I loved more than Him. I was hearing words that were different from the desires that had governed me before.

That experience answered the prayer I had prayed in the mountain in South Korea. I had asked Him to make me love Him, and something in my heart changed.

I do not mean that I ceased to be human or that no desire has ever approached my heart since. There are times when I can sense an attachment developing and know that I must give something up. But from that day, a change had taken place in what I wanted most.

When I later resigned from my job, there were other attractive opportunities. There were further offers of employment and proposals to increase my salary. Yet those offers could not become the deciding thing for me.

I understand comfort and the good things of life. I believe in God's blessing. The issue is the heart's attachment. What has the power to make you walk away from what God is saying?

God answered that prayer I prayed in South Korea: “Lord, I don't like You. I don't like Your things. I can see it's good, but it's not attractive to me. Make me love You.” The answer was what I heard myself saying on that winter morning. I'm sharing that with you to tell you that God can change your heart if you ask Him.
